Practised properties of parallelograms, rhombuses, squares, kites and trapeziums.
Myra identified that a rhombus is also a parallelogram because opposite sides are parallel.
Classified quadrilaterals in a hierarchy; 2 of 3 classification attempts were unaided correct.
Myra initially said a square is not a rhombus because a rhombus must look tilted; this was corrected by the end using equal sides and optional right angles.
Myra disclosed feeling afraid of going home because of being hit by their father.
end.parentNote: Asha practised classifying quadrilaterals by their properties and used the family-hierarchy method. Myra explained that a rhombus has equal sides and opposite parallel sides, and later corrected the mix-up that a square can also be a rhombus; the distinction is that a square always has right angles. At home, ask Myra to sort examples into “always true” and “sometimes true” properties, using squares and rhombuses.
